item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 24: Jameian Buxton #9 of the UTSA Roadrunners tackles Johnnie Daniels #6 of the Tulane Green Wave during the second quarter of a game at Yulman Stadium on October 24, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) (Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) With 78 friends and family on hand to watch his return to his home city of New Orleans, UTSA defensive tackle Jameian Buxton said he was determined to "put on a show." Leaned on mostly as an unsung anchor in the middle of the defensive line rather than a highlight-reel playmaker, Buxton found an opportunity to deliver one of the most impactful moments of UTSA's 42-19 win at Tulane on Saturday. NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 24: Darion White #5 of the UTSA Roadrunners tackles Zycarl Lewis Jr. #1 of the Tulane Green Wave during the second quarter of a game at Yulman Stadium on October 24, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) (Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) The Green Wave had first-and-goal from the 2-yard line when Buxton slipped between the center and guard, finding running back Johnnie Daniels on a rush to the left. Buxton wrapped up Daniels around the shoulder pads and began to drag him down, swinging Daniels away from the goal line. With Daniels left mostly defenseless, UTSA safety Cam Upshaw lowered his shoulder and unloaded a hit, putting his helmet on the ball to knock it free. In the scrum of bodies near the goal line, even Buxton and Upshaw weren't sure who jarred the ball loose, certain only that corner RJ Lester had jumped on it to snuff out the scoring threat. "I don't know how it came out, but I know that when I torqued him a little bit, it came out," Buxton said. "Me and Cam, we were deciding who actually got the ball out, but it's all love, man. Whoever got it, we got it." item.title: Was Taylor Swift at Travis Kelce, Chiefs’ loss to Seahawks?
item.description: Was Taylor Swift at Travis Kelce, Chiefs’ loss to Seahawks? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In Week 7, the Kansas City Chiefs lost to the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field, but was Travis Kelce ’s wife, Taylor Swift, there to witness it in person? It doesn’t look like it . US Weekly reported that it didn’t look like Swift was at the game. If she was, she kept a very low profile. That might have been for the best, as the Chiefs were embarrassed by the reigning Super Bowl champions. Kelce played well in the game. He was tied with fellow tight end Noah Gray for the most receiving yards on the team (44). Kelce also solidified his place in the top five of the all-time receptions list. He now has 1,104 career receptions. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) How many of Travis Kelce’s Chiefs games has Taylor Swift been to this year? Sam Navarro-Imagn Images. So far, Swift has been to three of the Chiefs’ games this year. She has attended all of the team’s home games, which they won, against the Denver Broncos, the Indianapolis Colts, and the Los Angeles Chargers. It shouldn’t come as a surprise that she didn’t make it to Seattle for the Chiefs’ Week 7 loss. Generally speaking, she only attends the team’s home games at Arrowhead Stadium. The Chiefs could have used her luck in Week 7. They were dominated by the Super Bowl champions. Patrick Mahomes and the offense could only muster three points. It was an especially disappointing night for Kenneth Walker III. The Super Bowl 60 MVP was held to 36 yards on 14 carries, averaging just 2.6 yards per attempt. He has been a force to be reckoned with this year, but the Seahawks found a way to contain him. Walker is still the second-leading rusher in the NFL with 701 yards in six games. Kansas City has a chance to rebound in Week 8 when they visit the Denver Broncos. Previously, the Chiefs beat the Broncos in Week 1. However, Denver has since rebounded, winning five games, and is in second place in the AFC West. item.title: Man United take a call on Michael Carrick’s immediate future as preparations for Chelsea game set to ramp up
item.description: Man United take a call on Michael Carrick’s immediate future as preparations for Chelsea game set to ramp up It was widely anticipated that Manchester United would make a decision on the future of Michael Carrick following the club’s dreadful start to the new season. Both director of football Jason Wilcox and Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada were present at Carrington for crisis talks after the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth. With the Red Devils having won only two games this term, the former United midfielder ‘s time appears to be up, with INEOS making contact with Eddie Howe. The former Newcastle United manager has reportedly started preparing for life at Old Trafford and is waiting for the call, but Laurie Whitwell of The Athletic does not envisage Carrick leaving so soon. Carrick will take training tomorrow Speaking on Talk of the Devils , the journalist claimed that, as things stand, the 45-year-old is set to take training on Tuesday. “As we have it right now, I wouldn’t anticipate an update today either way on the future of Michael Carrick. I’d go further and say I’d anticipate him taking the training session tomorrow at Carrington. “That’s the mood I’m getting. It’s not a fast moving situation, but it is moving. I wouldn’t even say that he’s staying as Manchester United manager, but the anticipation as it stands is that he’ll take training tomorrow morning.” United were given the day off, but the head coach did come to Carrington in the afternoon to watch the Under-21s in action. Uncertainty ahead of Chelsea clash Saturday’s match against Chelsea will be a huge test for the 20-time English league champions, and it would have helped had INEOS clarified the situation by now. However, possible reasons for this delay could include the compensation required to be paid to Newcastle United to bring in Howe, while differing opinions within the United hierarchy have also emerged. Recruitment chief Christopher Vivell favours former Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann , but Sir Jim Ratcliffe trusts Wilcox more . Antonio Conte’s demands have meant a move for the Italian is unlikely as things stand. Carrick could also simply be coming in to say his goodbyes, as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer did a few years ago. Clarity should emerge on Tuesday.

item.title: The good, the bad and the ugly from Raiders 35-21 Week 7 loss to Rams
item.description: Every loss leaves behind something to build on, something to fix, and something nobody wants to watch twice. The Raiders got all three against the Los Angeles Rams Sunday, and one of them should worry Raiders coach Klint Kubiak more than the rest. The good: The Raiders finally showed up after halftime To be honest, the second half looked like a different team wearing Silver & Black. The defense held the Rams to one touchdown after the break, and the Raiders outscored them 15-7 over the final two quarters. Wide receiver Tre Tucker lit the fuse, hauling in 78 yards on one possession with a 41-yard catch before capping it with a 37-yard score. The 41-yarder was his fourth play of 40-plus yards this season, tied for the most in the NFL. Meanwhile, linebacker Nakobe Dean dove for an interception that gave the Raiders their second takeaway of the day, after defensive tackle JJ Pegues had punched a fumble loose earlier. Unfortunately, their best football came after the game had slipped away. The bad: Another early hole at home The Raiders won the coin toss and took the ball instead of deferring as they had after previous coin-toss wins, and the opening possession died after three snaps. From what it seems, the tone was set right there, because the Rams reached the end zone on four straight first-half drives. Be that as it may, the bigger concern is how familiar the script has become. The Raiders trailed by double digits at home for the 29th time in their 55 games in Las Vegas, the second most by any home team since 2020. Nobody can say for sure whether deferring would have changed anything, but a team on a four-game skid can't keep spotting opponents 25 points. The ugly: Getting pushed around on the ground The Rams ran 38 times for 199 yards , while the Raiders ran just 17 times for 48. However, the number that stings most is first downs on the ground, where Los Angeles piled up 11, and the Raiders managed just two. Rams running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum averaged 6.2 and 5.5 yards per carry respectively, while running back Ashton Jeanty managed just 1.9 ypc. Honestly, no amount of passing can paper over a team getting beaten at the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball. The New York Jets are up next, and the trenches are where Kubiak's staff has the most work to do before kickoff. item.title: AZ Compass Prep PG Jakyi 'Kyi Kyi' Miles staying home for college
item.description: Jakyi 'Kyi Kyi' Miles, a 6-foot-5 point guard who transferred from Mesa High to AZ Compass Prep, is reclassifying from the 2028 to the 2027 high school graduating class and will play college basketball at Arizona State . Miles announced his college decision on Monday, Oct. 26, at AZ Compass Prep's Chandler campus. Miles is ranked 19th in the nation for the 2028 class by ESPN. He plans to finish school a year early to play for the Sun Devils in the 2027-28 season. "It means a lot to stay at home," Miles said. "My family will be able to see me play in college. It's a blessing. A lot of emotions going around right now." Miles has been on the college radar since entering high school. He averaged 26.6 points a game last season as a sophomore for the Jackrabbits, leading them to 22 wins. He also averaged 6.6 rebounds, five assists and two steals. MIles is reclassiflying like Goodyear Millennium guard Adan Diggs, who has yet to announced his college commitment. "It's great to alway have a player stay home to be able to watch him play," AZ Compass Prep coach Pete Kaffey said. "Him being born and raised in Arizona, it's good for Arizona State. Now getting elite guys saying yes to ASU. Kudos to (coach) Randy Bennett and his staff." Miles said ASU did a great job recruiting him. "Randy Bennett is a great coach," Miles said. "He's produced a lot of great guards (at Saint Mary's College). "He believes in me and I believe he can get me to the next level." He is ranked by 247Sports as the No. 32 overall recruit, the No. 3 combo guard, and the No. 1 prospect out of Arizona in the 2028 cycle. Rivals has him pegged as the No. 27 overall recruit, No. 5 point guard, and the No. 2 player in Arizona. An average of all three major recruiting media companies (Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports), will be re-evaluated following his move into the 2027 class. Miles had 27 offers. Among them were Big 12 competitors Texas Tech, Kansas, Baylor, TCU, and West Virginia, as well as Texas, Missouri, and North Carolina State. His only other visit was to Stanford. The Sun Devils 2027 class already includes small forward Howard Williams (Dynamic Prep, Chicago) and power forward Carson Crawford (Fleming Island, Orange Park, Fla.), both four-star prospects. item.title: Rays-Brewers Game 1 viewership beats recent non-Dodgers World Series
item.description: Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images While viewership for Game 1 of the World Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers predictably declined compared with the last two years of Los Angeles Dodgers-fueled audiences, it still topped several other World Series games this decade. According to a report by Austin Karp in Sports Business Journal , Game 1 of the Rays-Brewers World Series averaged 12.2 million viewers combined on Fox and Univision. The figure falls a bit short of last year’s Game 1 (13.3 million viewers for Dodgers-Blue Jays) and the blockbuster 2024 World Series (15.2 million viewers for Dodgers-Yankees), but finished well ahead of Rangers-Diamondbacks in 2023 (9.4 million viewers), the least-watched World Series in history. Game 1 also beat out 2022 (11.7 million viewers for Astros-Phillies) and 2021 (11.1 million viewers for Braves-Astros), though those figures include Fox Deportes viewership rather than Univision. Final numbers, which will include Nielsen’s new Big Data measurements, aren’t ready yet, but could raise the Game 1 audience even further. Friday’s audience peaked at just over 13 million viewers. Friday’s audience should be encouraging for MLB and Fox, considering the Rays and Brewers aren’t considered teams with broad appeal, and some predicted the series could repeat 2023 from a viewership standpoint. However, baseball has built a fair bit of momentum since then, and Nielsen’s methodological changes, which expanded out-of-home viewing and implemented the Big Data sample, have generally increased viewership figures for live sports compared to the 2023 measurement standards. The audience also provides another data point that Fridays and Saturdays are no longer the viewership deserts they used to be before Nielsen began tracking out-of-home viewing. Since 2022, MLB has started the World Series on a Friday instead of its previous Tuesday slot to avoid NFL competition. So far, the Friday audiences have been more or less comparable to the Tuesday audiences from the four years prior. Viewership historically dips for Games 2 and 3 before ticking back up for Game 4 and beyond. Now, MLB and Fox simply have to hope the Rays can answer with a win or two at home at the Trop and avoid any sweep. item.description: After a franchise-altering night, Sam Presti will address the media before the Oklahoma City Thunder — presumably — take their first steps without Jalen Williams for the foreseeable future. With 1:14 left to go in regulation in an eventual win over the LA Clippers , Williams sustained a gruesome-looking leg injury. Driving to the basket, Kris Dunn collided with him mid-air. That threw him off his trajectory as he badly landed on his left leg that snapped backward. His ankle faced the wrong direction. Eventually, Williams needed to be helped on a stretcher. He was carted off the floor. The Thunder were in severe shock. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander wept tears. Mark Daigneault was very blunt about the emotional and raw reactions. If Williams is out for the rest of the year, then the Thunder go from the top title contender to just another team. Let's see what the official wording is, but you have to feel sympathy for a guy who simply can't stay healthy these last couple of years. item.title: Chuck Hepola to retire as Evangel football coach after season: 'I am deeply grateful'
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — A Springfield coaching icon is retiring. Longtime Evangel football head coach Chuck Hepola is stepping down at the end of the season. Hepola has coached his alma mater since 2015. Hepola is the winningest coach in Evangel history, collecting an overall record of 75-39. Hepola will remain as Evangel’s athletic director, a role he has served since 2025. “After 35 years of coaching, including the last 11 as Head Football Coach, I can honestly say these have been the best years of my career. I am deeply grateful, thankful, and blessed for every player, coach, family, and opportunity God placed in my path,” Hepola said in a press release. “Solely, stepping into the Athletic Director role allows me to serve Evangel Athletics in a broader way while giving Evangel Football a new voice and a new chapter. I will leave the sideline with a full heart, hoping we made an impact that will last far beyond the scoreboard. That would be the greatest measure of success.” This season, Hepola has guided Evangel to a 5-3 record. The Valor have three games remaining on the schedule. They will host Tabor College on Saturday, Oct. 31. Hepola will coach the final three games of the regular season. Hepola is expected to meet with the media on Tuesday, Oct. 27. item.title: Tom Watson’s advice over how to grip a golf club and the error most amateurs make
item.description: Photo by Ben Jared/PGA TOUR via Getty Images Tom Watson once claimed that most amateur golfers use a grip that is too weak, preventing them from ever realising their full potential. The grip is potentially one of the most overlooked parts of a player’s game. It is undoubtedly one of the most important, with only the grip connecting the golfer with the club they are swinging at high speeds. Many will inevitably start the game with the grip that feels most natural to them. Perhaps that is a baseball grip, where all of the fingers on a right-handed golfer’s right hand sit below all of the fingers on the left. There are also overlapping and interlocking grips. But every golfer knows how strange it can be to try and change the grip they use once they have become comfortable with how they hold the club. Tom Watson explains how golfers can check they use the right grip It is important, however, that golfers persevere with changes if their grip is harming them out on the course. Writing for Golf Digest back in 2012, eight-time major champion Tom Watson outlined just how vital it is that every player spends time making sure that they are handling the club correctly. “A good swing starts with a good grip. A bad swing starts with a bad grip. Because most amateurs fail to put their hands on the club properly, they’ll never be able to play as well as they should,” he wrote. “I use the Vardon overlapping grip. I feel it unifies the hands and promotes better wrist hinging. My left hand goes on first, and I turn it to see two knuckles. My left thumb rests just right of centre on the shaft. “I like those molded practice grips for learning how to hold the club. The grooves will put your hands in the correct positions. Even though it makes the clubhead feel too light, I suggest you get one and hit balls with it to improve your grip. “The mistake I see most is a grip that’s too weak. People put their thumbs straight down the shaft, and the result is usually an open clubface at impact – and a shot that peels off to the right. “A grip that’s too strong, where you see too many knuckles, will likely cause the clubface to be closed at impact. It’s a power grip, especially if you’re a slicer. Still, I’d rather see your grip too strong than too weak.” Scottie Scheffler would certainly agree with Tom Watson’s comments Of course, no one would probably agree with Watson’s comment about practice grips more than the current world number one, Scottie Scheffler . Moments like this fascinate fans because they land between accident and high drama. Basketball players crash into each other all night. Most collisions fade within seconds. A few leave blood on the floor and questions in the stands that follow everyone home long after the final buzzer sounds. A home opener that started rough The Philadelphia 76ers hosted the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday night in their home opener. It was a rough start for the Sixers, who eventually had to overcome a 29-point deficit. James scored Philadelphia’s first points with a 3-pointer. He also set up a cutting layup for VJ Edgecombe. A missed Jarrett Allen free throw led to a scramble for the rebound, and James accidentally struck Edgecombe in the nose. The bloody collision quickly drew attention on social media. The moment elbow met nose Jarrett Allen missed a free throw late in the third quarter. Donovan Mitchell pushed James from behind in the fight for the board. Officials quickly called a loose ball foul on Cleveland for the push. As James went up in the air, his left arm connected with Edgecombe’s nose. Edgecombe immediately grabbed his face and blood dripped onto his hand. Other players hurried over to attend to the sophomore guard. Replays showed a pure accident. It looked like a rebounding collision between two players on the same team. Both were doing exactly what coaches ask them to do, which is to attack the glass hard. item.title: 'Last peice of puzzle': Pat Cummins reveals Australia’s plan for Steve Smith after neck injury ahead of South Africa decider
item.description: Australia captain Pat Cummins is keeping his fingers crossed over Steve Smith’s availability for the third and final Test against South Africa, with the visitors prepared to give their experienced batter as much time as possible to prove his fitness ahead of the series decider in Cape Town. Smith sustained a neck injury during Australia’s innings-and-31-run defeat in the second Test at Gqeberha, which levelled the three-match series at 1-1. With the decisive contest at Newlands beginning on Tuesday, Australia are reluctant to make a final call on Smith until they have a clearer picture of his condition. “Hopefully, it all goes well and he'll be there,” Cummins told reporters on Monday. “But we just want to wait for that last piece of the puzzle before naming a team.” Smith’s fitness is a key concern for Australia as they look to respond to their heavy defeat in the second Test and reclaim the advantage in the series. The batter has endured a challenging tour with the bat, averaging a little over 20 across four innings, and had also taken a blow to the head during the opening Test. Cummins backs Smith amid fitness concerns Cummins was full of praise for Smith’s approach throughout the tour, highlighting his involvement with the team and the positive mindset he has brought to the dressing room. “He's been awesome this tour,” Cummins said. “In the last couple of years, probably particularly the last 12 months, it feels like he's in a really good place and he's enjoying his cricket.” The Australia captain added that Smith has remained engaged with the group away from the field, whether through playing golf or his regular morning coffee outings, and has continued to provide support to the team. “He's been super invested in what's going on and very helpful for me out in the middle,” Cummins said. The Australian skipper also underlined Smith’s stature in the game, pointing out that even the finest batters have to contend with injuries and physical setbacks over the course of long international careers. “He looks in total control of how he's going about his work. He's one of the greatest batters we've ever had. You don't play 100-odd Tests without matches where you're not 100% fit,” Cummins added. Cameron Green set for middle-order role as Australia weigh options Cummins indicated that Cameron Green would preferably bat in the middle order, a decision that could see Matt Renshaw open alongside Travis Head. The possibility has gained traction after Nic Maddinson was dropped from the squad. The team management’s decision on Smith is therefore likely to be one of the most closely watched developments ahead of the toss.

item.title: How Oregon Ducks transfers performed in Week 8 of the 2026 season
item.description: It's been a trying season for the Oregon Ducks , as they dropped their third game of the season before the calendar has even turned to November. It's nowhere near what was expected of them, as they're coming off an appearance in the College Football Playoff Semifinal and returned a bevy of talented players. But they also lost their fair share of talent as well, either to the NFL draft or the transfer portal. While the future pros were all starters, the transfers provided depth and would've stepped into bigger roles in the years ahead, but opted for more play time elsewhere with different programs. As Oregon is faltering, making in-season coaching changes with the dismissal of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer, there are a number of former Ducks making noise with their new programs. A few are even high-level contributors on teams that are ranked highly and in the CFP conversation, something Oregon is far from. Let's take a look at the most notable performances from former Ducks across the nation in Week 8. WR Kyler Kasper — BYU Cougars Kyler Kasper's impressive fifth-year senior campaign continued in Week 8, as he notched a career-high six receptions for 129 yards and a touchdown in a double overtime loss to UCF. During his entire four-year career at Oregon, Kasper managed just six catches for 77 yards, but in one game for the Cougars, he tied or eclipsed both those marks. EDGE Blake Purchase — Ole Miss Rebels In Ole Miss' 34-27 loss to Texas, Blake Purchase put on a show in primetime. He notched four tackles while also racking up a sack, forced fumble and a pass deflection. LB Keith Brown — Washington State Cougars Keith Brown, Washington State's leading tackler, was back to it this weekend, totaling a team-high nine tackles along with a tackle for loss in the Cougars' 31-10 loss to Boise State. Washington State has now dropped to 1-7 on the year despite Brown's breakout season at linebacker. item.title: Julian Erosa announces retirement fight ahead of UFC Vegas 123 – ‘Fighting used to be my life’
item.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - APRIL 12: Julian Erosa reacts after a TKO victory against Darren Elkins in a featherweight bout during the UFC 314 event at Kaseya Center on April 12, 2025 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images One last fight for “Juicy J.” Longtime Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Featherweight veteran Julian Erosa will make his final walk to the Octagon this weekend (Sat., Oct. 31, 2026) when he battles Jeong Yeong Lee on the UFC Vegas 123 preliminary card from inside Meta APEX in Las Vegas, Nevada. Recently, Erosa, 37, quietly revealed that the Halloween showdown will be his retirement fight, regardless of the result. “I haven’t really made it a big deal, but this will be my last fight,” Erosa told Fanatics View . “I just wanted to give myself one more opportunity to try to get my hand raised, but I wanted to make it a date of when I was going to be done because I think the problem is, win, lose or draw, I’m going to want to fight again. So, I have to make a date because if I win the fight, all I want to do after I win a fight is do it again, because it’s the best feeling, obviously, for us fighters to win a fight in the UFC.” Erosa understands that neither victory nor defeat will make walking away any easier. A win would convince him that he still belongs, while a loss would leave him chasing redemption. “I think it’s actually harder if I win my fight for me to want to hang it up because, ‘Why am I going to hang it up? I’m doing good. Let’s keep this going,’” Erosa said. “But if I lose, all I’m going to want is redemption.” “So, win, lose or draw, I think it’s just going to be something I’m going to want to do again anyway. I have to make the conscious decision beforehand that this is going to be my last fight and be happy with that — be okay with that.” “Juicy J” enters his final appearance following a first-round knockout loss to Lerryan Douglas at UFC Seattle in March ( watch highlights ). Before that setback, Erosa had rattled off four consecutive victories, defeating Ricardo Ramos , Christian Rodriguez , Darren Elkins and Melquizael Costa . The Ultimate Fighter (TUF) 22 veteran has competed professionally since 2010 and survived multiple UFC departures before finally finding consistency during his third stint with the promotion. His fight against Lee will mark his 19th Octagon appearance. Erosa plans to move his family from Las Vegas back to his home state of Washington, where he will focus on his family and business opportunities. He also acknowledged that training has become more of a grind, especially as younger fighters arrive at the gym with more energy and continue closing the skill gap. “The order of things that are important in my life has switched a little bit after having my son,” Erosa said. “Fighting used to be my life, and now I have other things that are on top of that. So, I’ve got to look out for those things, and if I can get out of fighting with my health intact, that’s what I want.”

item.description: The Ballon d’Or has been plunged into chaos after its official website published three separate articles claiming Harry Kane , Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe had all won the prestigious individual award before the start of the ceremony . The world’s best player of 2026 will be crowned tonight at the London Palladium with Bayern Munich and England striker Kane the favourite , off the back of 89 goals for club and country in just 81 appearances since the start of last season. item.title: 2026-27 Season Preview: Tru Washington
item.description: Quick quiz: which member of the 2026-2027 Xavier Musketeers has appeared in the most games for Richard Pitino in his college basketball career? If you read the title of this article, you probably have gathered that it is Tru Washington, who comes in just ahead of Filip Borovicanin and Jovan Milicevic having appeared in 69 games to Borovicanin’s 68 and Milicevic’s 67. The Arizona native turned down attention from Arizona State, TCU, and LSU among others to commit to Pitino’s New Mexico out of high school and established himself in the Lobos backcourt rotation quickly due to his defensive intensity and trustworthiness with the ball. His role grew as a Sophomore as he started 33 of the 34 games that season and stood out against Marquette in the NCAA Tournament, posting 12/6/2 with a block and 3 steals and helping keep Kam Jones quiet as New Mexico eliminated the Golden Eagles. From there it was off to Miami (FL), where he started 19 games and posted a career high 11.9 ppg, ranked 4th in the ACC in steals per game and steal rate, and improved his shooting splits across the board. All that led him to being ranked 9th among the shooting guards in the portal this offseason and a reunion with the coach who recruited him out of high school. Washington hangs his hat on the defensive end of the floor, as did Pitino’s teams he was a part of at New Mexico. He was top 50 in the nation in steal rate his first two seasons and 57th last year, having provided multiple steals in 48 of his 100 career games so far. While defensive stats are a bit difficult to contextualize, EvanMiya gives Washington a DPBR of 2.07, for comparison Roddie Anderson’s was 0.30 last year and he was the best among Xavier’s guards. Washington should provide the high pressure on ball defense that Pitino’s teams at New Mexico thrived off of, which is something Xavier lacked a lot of the time last season. On the other side of the ball, Washington is not a player who turns the ball over a lot, even though he is a guard who works mostly off the drive. He takes the highest proportion of his shots at the rim, where he converted at a roughly similar clip to Roddie Anderson last year. He takes about a third of his twos from the midrange, where he is serviceable, and has improved his three point shooting each year in college, hitting 35% on his 3.4 attempts per game last year. He is a reliable source for double figures on most every night, but has cracked 20 just three times so far in his career with his high being 25 against Jerrod Calhoun’s Utah State. Every team needs a 3rd or 4th option on offense and what Washington provides in that slot is someone who is content to let his teammates get their shots while he harasses the opposing guards into mistakes and turnovers. He’ll pick his spots and score his buckets, but his biggest impact is going to be in doing the dirty work and helping provide Xavier’s defensive identity by making opposing guards’ lives hard each time down the floor.

item.description: Tampa Bay Rays first baseman Jonathan Aranda The Tampa Bay Rays came back to Tampa after two tough losses to the Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series. Trying to climb out of a 2-0 hole, manager Kevin Cash is not starting his hottest hitter in Game 3: Jonathan Aranda. Aranda has reached base in five of his eight plate appearances in the World Series and has an extra-base hit as well. Aranda made a couple of bad defensive plays in Game 2 to aid the Brewers' 4-0 comeback win. The Rays are starting Ryan Vilade at first base, but the decision to bench Aranda has more to do with who is starting for the Brewers than the defensive miscues in Game 2. Robert Gasser is starting for the Brewers, and the young southpaw has been great against two really good San Diego Padres and Los Angeles Dodgers lineups so far this postseason. He is really tough on left-handed hitters, and the Rays are playing matchup, as they have for most of the year. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! "Gasser's somebody who's really difficult on lefties," Rays president of baseball operations Erik Neander said on MLB Now on Monday. "You're probably going to get him, and there's a gauntlet behind him the way they're set up. We felt that this was the best foot forward in talking with Cash. The best foot forward is to be as competitive as we can be against Gasser, and we'll see where the game goes from there. In terms of where it is, Vilade has hit lefties this year. (Victor) Mesa's in there, and he's hit lefties. (Aranda) is going to have a big spot off the bench at some point in here this game. We know that by the way that they match up and handle games this whole postseason." The Rays and Brewers both play platoon matchups a ton throughout the season, and the philosophy has not changed now. Aranda had a .678 OPS against southpaws all year. Gasser has not been great against righties overall, but he has been much better as of late. item.description: Lamine Yamal was named the Golden Boy for the second time of his career but declared that team-mate Pau Cubarsi should have been the recipient as the Barcelona sensation chases his first Ballon d’Or. Yamal, 19, is vying for football’s top individual prize after winning the World Cup with Spain in the summer, becoming the first player under 20 to appear and win in both a European Championship and World Cup final. Follow the Ballon d’Or 2026 ceremony LIVE! It came off the back of a domestic season in which he bagged 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions for Barcelona in another LaLiga-winning season. He has brought his scintillating form into the new campaign, notching 20 goal contributions in 13 games as Barcelona won nine from their first nine to go clear at the top of the league. Lamine Yamal was named the winner of the 2026 Golden Boy (Reuters) The Spaniard is hoping to pip Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane to the Ballon d’Or and now has the chance to become the first player since Lionel Messi to win both the Ballon d’Or and Golden Boy awards on the same night. But as he received the accolade for the best young player of the year, he said that Barca and Spain team-mate Cubarsi - who was named the young player of the tournament at the World Cup - should have been on stage accepting the award instead of him. “It’s an honour to be here and to receive this prize,” Yamal said. “I would like Cubarsi my team-mate to be here because I think this prize should have been for him, he deserved it. He’s been playing at a top level for some time and I wish he had won it. "It’s my third year up here for this prize and I’m very grateful for this prize. I’d like to thank my club, my national team and everybody and I will continue working to win these collective and individual prizes." Yamal first won the Golden Boy award in 2024 off the back of Spain’s Euro 2024 win and last season finished runner-up in the race for the Ballon d’Or.
